rules.title: Meghalaya: no Inner Line Permit at present
rules.detail: A hotel company's site says Indian citizens need only a valid identity card and foreign citizens register with the Foreigners Registration Office. No official page stating this was found.

source.title: ILP Requirement for Meghalaya - Do You Need a Permit?

rules.title: Meghalaya: compulsory visitor registration planned, not in force
rules.detail: Announced in July 2026 by the Tourism Minister: visitors would register and have identity checked on entry, first at Umling. No start date or legal basis was given.

source.title: Meghalaya plans mandatory registration for tourists, visitors on ILP lines

history.change: Plan announced, with Umling as the first registration point and Berubari in the Garo Hills to follow.

source.title: Meghalaya plans mandatory registration for tourists, visitors on ILP lines

history.change: An opposition party asked which law the registration would rest on; no start date reported.

source.title: Move for compulsory tourist registration on the anvil

rules.title: Meghalaya: stays must register every guest
rules.detail: Hotels, homestays and landlords register guests through the state tourism app, which is linked to the police. Reported June 2025; carry identity proof for check-in.

source.title: Here's Why Meghalaya Has Made Tourist Registration Mandatory At All Accommodations

history.change: Guest registration through the state tourism app made compulsory for all accommodation; reported 19 June 2025.

source.title: Here's Why Meghalaya Has Made Tourist Registration Mandatory At All Accommodations

rules.title: Meghalaya: renting out private motorcycles is prohibited
rules.detail: A Transport Department notice of 13 June 2025 bars renting private two-wheelers and cars, citing the Motor Vehicles Act. No rent-a-motorcycle scheme is notified in the state.
rules.applies_to: Riders planning to rent a motorcycle in Meghalaya
rules.set_by: Commissioner of Transport, Government of Meghalaya

rules.title: Dawki road: shut from 10 pm to 5 am
rules.detail: The night closure between Laitlyngkot and Lyngkyrdem stayed in force when the stretch reopened on 10 August 2026. Emergency vehicles may pass with clearance.

hazards.title: Rockfall and landslides on the Dawki road
hazards.detail: A rockslide at Mawlieh killed two people on 20 April 2026 and a landslide cut the road beyond Laitlyngkot in June. It reopened on 10 August.

hazards.detail: The tourism department tells visitors to check daily forecasts and heed warnings of heavy rain and landslides.

hazards.title: Avoid the Dawki road at night and after rain
hazards.detail: The August 2026 reopening notice advised against travel in heavy rain, just after rain, and at night.
